title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 17
paragraphs: While Mardonius was encamped in Boeotia, the rest of the Greeks who lived in these parts and took the Medes' side were all supplying troops and had joined in the invasion of Attica. Only the Phokians had not joined in the invasion — the Phokians, I say, for they too were now actively taking the side of the Medes, not of their own will but under compulsion. Not many days after Mardonius's arrival at Thebes, a thousand of their hoplites came, led by Harmokydes, the man of greatest repute among their citizens. When these too came to Thebes, Mardonius sent horsemen and bade the Phokians take up position by themselves in the plain. After they had done so, the whole cavalry suddenly appeared, and a rumor spread through the Greek army on the Median side that the cavalry was about to shoot them down with javelins; this same report went through the Phokians themselves. Then their commander Harmokydes exhorted them as follows: “Phokians, it is clear that these men mean to deliver us to an easily foreseen death, because we have been falsely accused by the Thessalians, I conjecture. Now, therefore, it is right that every one of you prove himself a good man, for it is better to end our lives performing deeds of valor and defending ourselves than to be destroyed by a dishonorable death as offered victims. Let each of them learn that they are barbarians, and we — against whom they devised murder — are Greeks.”
